basis: Tech.eu (2017-07-11): Wikimart 'was heavily funded by Western investors, with Tiger Global Management, investing some $30 million in total in 2010, 2011 and 2012'; Kommersant (2012-03-13): Tiger put $18M into the $30M round of March 2012 after $12M of the $13.2M the company had raised before. The entry is the company's first outside round (Russian Wikipedia: about $5M, late 2009), a financing of an 18-month-old startup; Tiger held about 55% after the 2012 round, so the control question is flagged for Erik in the note

note: Moscow online marketplace launched in June 2008. Tiger Global was its main outside investor: about $5M in late 2009 (Russian Wikipedia), $12M of the $13.2M raised by spring 2011, and $18M of a $30M round in March 2012 (Kommersant), after which it held about 55% (founders 23%); none of these rounds is named, so the stage is undetermined. FOR ERIK: Tiger became the majority owner through these financings (the 2012 stake, and 'more than 50%' sold to Finprombank's shareholders in October 2014, roem.ru), but the first cheque was a startup's first institutional round and no record says it gave control, so the row is kept a member under T3 rather than excluded as a control position; a ruling may move it. Tiger stopped funding after the 2014 sanctions (Tech.eu); the company stopped operating in December 2016 (Topnews) and went bankrupt: defunct.

funding_rounds.round: Follow-on (not named); $12M of $13.2M raised came from Tiger
